_about: Curated team content for the Race Centre Teams page. Lineage follows the same factory and entry, so titles and wins of predecessor teams count (with the years each name raced). Title counts and wins are not typed here: python -m ingest.teams computes them from Jolpica results into team_stats.json. Colours are plain approximations; no logos or official assets.

teams.name: Mercedes
teams.lineage_note: The 1954-55 Mercedes-Benz works team was a separate operation from Stuttgart and is not counted here.

timeline.title: Tyrrell builds its own car
timeline.text: Ken Tyrrell's team, champions with a Matra chassis in 1969, debuts its first in-house car late in the season.

timeline.title: Double champions
timeline.text: Jackie Stewart wins the Drivers' title and Tyrrell takes the Constructors' Championship.

timeline.title: British American Racing
timeline.text: BAR buys Tyrrell and races from the Brackley factory under its own name.

timeline.title: Honda takes over
timeline.text: Honda runs the team as its works entry; Jenson Button wins the rain-hit Hungarian Grand Prix.

timeline.title: Brawn GP's one perfect season
timeline.text: Rescued after Honda's exit, Brawn GP wins both championships with Jenson Button in its only year.

timeline.title: Mercedes arrives
timeline.text: Mercedes buys Brawn GP, and Michael Schumacher comes out of retirement to drive for it.

timeline.title: The hybrid era begins
timeline.text: The new turbo-hybrid rules start a run of eight straight Constructors' titles, from 2014 to 2021.

timeline.title: Seven titles
timeline.text: Lewis Hamilton wins his seventh Drivers' title, equalling Michael Schumacher's record.

timeline.title: Present from the start
timeline.text: Ferrari enters the first season of the World Championship and is the only team to have raced in every season since.

timeline.title: First win
timeline.text: José Froilán González beats the Alfa Romeos at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone.

timeline.title: Ascari's double
timeline.text: Alberto Ascari wins back-to-back Drivers' titles in 1952 and 1953.

timeline.title: America's first champion
timeline.text: Phil Hill becomes the first American World Champion, driving for Ferrari.

timeline.title: Lauda's first title
timeline.text: Niki Lauda wins the Drivers' Championship and Ferrari the Constructors'.

timeline.title: Scheckter's crown
timeline.text: Jody Scheckter wins the title, starting a 21-year wait for Ferrari's next Drivers' champion.

timeline.title: The Schumacher era
timeline.text: Michael Schumacher wins the first of five consecutive Drivers' titles with Ferrari, from 2000 to 2004.

timeline.title: Räikkönen by a point
timeline.text: Kimi Räikkönen wins the championship by a single point at the final race in Brazil.

teams.name: McLaren
teams.lineage_note: In the early years results are filed under the car-engine name (McLaren-Ford, McLaren-BRM and others); all are the same team.

timeline.title: Bruce McLaren's team
timeline.text: Founder Bruce McLaren gives the team its World Championship debut at the Monaco Grand Prix.

timeline.title: First win
timeline.text: Bruce McLaren wins the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa in a car carrying his own name.

timeline.title: First titles
timeline.text: Emerson Fittipaldi wins the Drivers' Championship and McLaren its first Constructors' title.

timeline.title: 15 wins from 16
timeline.text: Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost win all but one race of the season.

timeline.title: Häkkinen's double
timeline.text: Mika Häkkinen wins the first of back-to-back titles in 1998 and 1999.

timeline.title: Hamilton by a point
timeline.text: Lewis Hamilton wins his first title by one point on the final lap in Brazil.

timeline.title: Back on top
timeline.text: McLaren wins the Constructors' Championship for the first time since 1998.

timeline.title: Norris is champion
timeline.text: Lando Norris wins the Drivers' title at the final race in Abu Dhabi.

timeline.title: Stewart Grand Prix
timeline.text: Jackie Stewart and his son Paul start the team that later becomes Red Bull Racing.

timeline.title: Stewart's only win
timeline.text: Johnny Herbert wins a chaotic European Grand Prix at the Nürburgring.

timeline.title: Jaguar Racing
timeline.text: Ford rebrands the team as Jaguar for five seasons.

timeline.title: Red Bull buys in
timeline.text: The energy drink company buys Jaguar's team and races as Red Bull Racing.

timeline.title: First win
timeline.text: Sebastian Vettel wins a wet Chinese Grand Prix for the team's first victory.

timeline.title: Four in a row
timeline.text: Vettel and Red Bull win both championships every year from 2010 to 2013.

timeline.title: Verstappen's first title
timeline.text: Max Verstappen wins the championship at the final race in Abu Dhabi.

timeline.title: 21 wins from 22
timeline.text: Red Bull wins every Grand Prix but one, a record for a single season.

timeline.title: Minardi debuts
timeline.text: Giancarlo Minardi's small Faenza team starts a 21-season run as the grid's favourite underdog.

timeline.title: Scuderia Toro Rosso
timeline.text: Red Bull buys Minardi and turns it into its second team, for young drivers.

timeline.title: Vettel's Monza miracle
timeline.text: Sebastian Vettel wins a wet Italian Grand Prix from pole, the team's first win.

timeline.title: A 17-year-old debut
timeline.text: Max Verstappen makes his Formula 1 debut with Toro Rosso.

timeline.title: AlphaTauri wins at Monza
timeline.text: Renamed AlphaTauri, the team wins the Italian Grand Prix again, with Pierre Gasly.

timeline.title: RB
timeline.text: The team is renamed again as Red Bull's second outfit enters a new era.

teams.name: Alpine
teams.lineage_note: Renault's own 1977-85 works team was a separate operation and is not counted here.

timeline.title: Toleman arrives
timeline.text: The Witney-based Toleman team enters Formula 1 and, after months of failing to qualify, starts its first race at Monza.

timeline.title: Senna's rookie podium
timeline.text: In his rookie season, Ayrton Senna finishes second at a rain-soaked Monaco.

timeline.title: Benetton's first win
timeline.text: Renamed Benetton, the team wins the Mexican Grand Prix with Gerhard Berger.

timeline.title: Schumacher's first titles
timeline.text: Michael Schumacher wins the Drivers' Championship in 1994 and 1995, and Benetton the 1995 Constructors'.

timeline.title: Renault takes over
timeline.text: Renault, owner since 2000, renames the team and races it under its own name from Enstone.

timeline.title: Alonso ends the Ferrari run
timeline.text: Fernando Alonso and Renault win both championships in 2005 and 2006.

timeline.title: Lotus F1
timeline.text: Racing as Lotus, the team wins the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix with Kimi Räikkönen.

timeline.title: Alpine's first win
timeline.text: Esteban Ocon wins a chaotic Hungarian Grand Prix in the team's first year as Alpine.

timeline.title: Points on debut
timeline.text: Gene Haas's team arrives, and Romain Grosjean finishes sixth in its very first race in Australia.

timeline.title: Best season
timeline.text: Haas finishes fifth in the Constructors' Championship, its best result.

timeline.title: First pole
timeline.text: Kevin Magnussen takes a surprise pole position in changing conditions in Brazil.

timeline.title: New leadership
timeline.text: Ayao Komatsu replaces Guenther Steiner as team principal.

teams.name: Audi
teams.lineage_note: Alfa Romeo's own works teams of the 1950s and 1979-85 were separate operations and are not counted here.

timeline.title: Sauber enters Formula 1
timeline.text: Peter Sauber's team scores points on its debut, with JJ Lehto fifth in South Africa.

timeline.title: BMW Sauber
timeline.text: BMW buys the team and runs it as its works entry.

timeline.title: Kubica's win
timeline.text: Robert Kubica wins the Canadian Grand Prix, leading a one-two with Nick Heidfeld.

timeline.title: Back to Sauber
timeline.text: BMW leaves and Peter Sauber buys back the team he founded.

timeline.title: Alfa Romeo name
timeline.text: The team races as Alfa Romeo for five seasons.

timeline.title: Audi's works team
timeline.text: Audi takes full ownership and makes its Formula 1 debut with its own power unit.

teams.name: Williams
teams.lineage_note: Frank Williams Racing Cars (1969-76) was an earlier, separate team that became Wolf; Williams Grand Prix Engineering first raced its own car in 1978.

timeline.title: Williams Grand Prix Engineering
timeline.text: Frank Williams and Patrick Head found the team, running a customer March car in its first season.

timeline.title: First win
timeline.text: Clay Regazzoni wins the British Grand Prix at Silverstone.

timeline.title: First titles
timeline.text: Alan Jones wins the Drivers' Championship and Williams its first Constructors' title.

timeline.title: Mansell's season
timeline.text: Nigel Mansell dominates in the active-suspension FW14B to win the title.

timeline.title: Villeneuve is champion
timeline.text: Jacques Villeneuve wins the Drivers' title after a final-race showdown at Jerez.

timeline.title: Maldonado in Spain
timeline.text: Pastor Maldonado wins the Spanish Grand Prix from pole.

timeline.title: End of the family era
timeline.text: The Williams family sells the team to Dorilton Capital.

teams.name: Aston Martin
teams.lineage_note: The 1959-60 Aston Martin works team was a separate operation and is not counted here.

timeline.title: Jordan Grand Prix
timeline.text: Eddie Jordan's team debuts, and Michael Schumacher makes his Formula 1 debut in its car at Spa.

timeline.title: One-two at Spa
timeline.text: Damon Hill leads Ralf Schumacher home in a wet Belgian Grand Prix for Jordan's first win.

timeline.title: Best season
timeline.text: Heinz-Harald Frentzen wins twice and Jordan finishes third in the Constructors' Championship.

timeline.title: Force India
timeline.text: After Midland and Spyker, the team becomes Force India.

timeline.title: Rescued
timeline.text: A consortium led by Lawrence Stroll saves the team and renames it Racing Point.

timeline.title: Pérez wins in Sakhir
timeline.text: Sergio Pérez recovers from last place on the first lap to win the Sakhir Grand Prix.

timeline.title: Aston Martin
timeline.text: The team takes the Aston Martin name.

timeline.title: Alonso joins
timeline.text: Fernando Alonso finishes on the podium in his first race for the team, in Bahrain.

timeline.title: An 11th team
timeline.text: Formula 1 approves a new American team backed by General Motors, the grid's first expansion since 2016.

timeline.title: Debut season
timeline.text: Cadillac makes its debut with Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Pérez.
